moduleTitle: Saving data to a system of record
learningObjectives: Configure a savable Data Page with the correct data save options to write data back to a system of record.
Trigger the save plan using a Save Data Page Automation Step and configure explicit or implicit Data Page references.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Savable Data Pages — Purpose and Configuration

elements.text: A savable Data Page is like a shared spreadsheet with a 'Submit' button. Users edit values in memory (the spreadsheet). Nothing hits the system of record until someone clicks Submit (triggers the save plan). If the submit fails halfway — say the network drops — transaction handling rolls back both sides so neither system ends up in a half-updated state.

elements.description: Pushes data FROM a Data Page TO a System of Record (SOR). Works for both Pega Platform's internal database and external SORs. Edit mode must be set to 'Savable'. A data save plan specifies how and where data is saved.

Pega's built-in transaction handling ensures that if any part of the save fails (e.g., network outage), the entire operation rolls back. Both the Pega side and the SOR side return to their pre-update state — no partial commits.

elements.term: When Conditions in the data save plan
elements.description: Configure When Conditions on each save target to commit to multiple data tables simultaneously. If a When Condition is true → the data commit runs. If all When Conditions are false → the Otherwise Condition runs.

Saves a single page to one database row in the internal SOR. Requires a Data Transform to map data before persistence. Supports page structure ONLY (not list). Ensures transactional integrity — the entire save succeeds or fails as a unit.

elements.term: Save options: Database update and Database delete
elements.description: Database update: modifies an existing record in the internal SOR within the same transaction scope. Database delete: removes a record from the internal SOR.
Saves data to an external SOR using REST-based integration. REST ONLY — not SOAP. Use when the external system exposes a REST API.

elements.term: Save options: Robotic Automation and Robotic Desktop Automation
elements.description: Robotic Automation: unattended RPA to write to an external system. Robotic Desktop Automation: desktop-driven RDA for UI-based external systems that have no API.
Custom persistence logic via an Activity Rule. Limit its use when possible — prefer the other dedicated options for standard integration patterns.

elements.term: Update vs. Create — key and source
elements.description: Updating: key IS PRESENT → use Lookup as source. Creating: key NOT PRESENT → use Data Transform as source. One savable Data Page supports BOTH via conditional sourcing — Lookup when a record exists; Data Transform when it doesn't.

elements.term: Auto-populated property + savable Data Page: must REFER, not Copy
elements.description: Use 'Refer to a Data Page' — not 'Copy data'. Copying snapshots the data; later user edits are invisible to the save plan and won't reach the SOR. Referring keeps a live connection so edits flow through.
Provides a simple way to update data object information without complex configuration. Supports additional validation and pre/post-processing of data.

elements.term: 3 ways to trigger the save plan
elements.description: ① Add a Save Data Page Automation Step in a flow (AFTER an Assignment). ② Add post-processing for a Flow Action. ③ Call Save-DataPage in an Activity. When triggered from a flow or Flow Action, Pega manages transaction handling automatically.

Place the Save Data Page Automation Step AFTER an Assignment Step in the flow. This ensures data is saved to the SOR after the user has entered or updated information. Placing it before would save stale or empty data.

elements.term: Multiple SOR commits in one flow
elements.description: To commit to multiple data sources, add MULTIPLE Save Data Page Automation Steps to the flow — one per SOR. A single step commits to only one data source.

elements.term: Explicit vs. Implicit Data Page reference
elements.description: Explicit: enter the Data Page Name directly — any parameters can be specified. Implicit ('Use associated property'): select a property whose associated savable Data Page is resolved automatically. Both allow adding an Audit Note.

examPitfalls.title: Savable Data Pages work for BOTH Pega Platform and external SORs
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which save target requires a Savable Data Page. Candidates answer 'external systems only,' not realizing a Savable Data Page also writes to the internal Pega Platform database via the Database save option.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Savable Data Pages push data to ANY system of record — internal Pega Platform database or external systems. The save plan's save option (Database save, Connector, etc.) determines the target.

examPitfalls.title: Connector data save option uses REST ONLY — not SOAP
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario describes a SOAP web service and asks which save option to use. Candidates select 'Connector' because the target is external. Connector is REST-only — SOAP requires a different approach.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Connector save option works with REST-based integrations ONLY. SOAP or other protocols require a different approach (e.g., Activity).

examPitfalls.title: Database save: page structure only, requires Data Transform mapping
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether a Save Data Page step automatically writes all clipboard properties to the database. Candidates say yes. The database save writes the PAGE STRUCTURE — each clipboard property must be explicitly mapped to a database column via a Data Transform.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Database save writes a single page to one database row. It supports page structure ONLY (not list). A Data Transform is required to map the response to the Data Model.

examPitfalls.title: Auto-populated property + savable Data Page: must REFER — not Copy
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how to set a Case property so that saving the Data Page also saves the property value. Candidates say 'use Copy data.' When an auto-populated property needs to be persisted via a savable Data Page, you must REFER to the Data Page property — copying creates a snapshot that is not connected to the savable page.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Must use 'Refer to a Data Page'. Copying creates a snapshot — edits made afterward are invisible to the save plan and won't be pushed to the SOR. Referring keeps the live connection.

examPitfalls.title: Update = Lookup (key present); Create = Data Transform (key absent)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes a savable Data Page handling both new and existing records. Candidates use Data Transform for both paths. Lookup (not Data Transform) handles the update path when the record key is already present.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Key present → Lookup (update existing). Key absent → Data Transform (create new). One savable Data Page supports both via conditional sourcing.

examPitfalls.title: Save Data Page Step goes AFTER an Assignment — not before
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where in the Case Life Cycle to place the Save Data Page Step. Candidates place it before the Assignment. The Save Data Page Step must be placed AFTER the Assignment that collects the data — placing it before means no user data has been entered yet.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Save Data Page Automation Step must come AFTER an Assignment. Placing it before saves stale or empty data to the SOR before the user enters anything.

examPitfalls.title: Multiple SOR commits require multiple Save Data Page Steps
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario requires writing to two external systems in one flow. Candidates add one Save Data Page Step expecting it to commit to both. One Save Data Page Step = exactly one SOR commit — two targets need two Steps.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: One Save Data Page Step = one SOR commit. To commit to two external systems, add two separate Save Data Page Automation Steps in the flow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to write updated HR seat assignment data from a Pega Case to an external database. Which Data Page edit mode is required?

options.text: Savable — enables a save plan to push Data Page contents to a system of record
Editable — allows the application to modify the Data Page contents in memory
Read-Only — streams data to the external system automatically
Requestor — persists data across all of the user's Cases

practiceQuiz.hint: Writing back to a SOR requires Savable mode.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Savable mode enables a data save plan that pushes Data Page contents to a SOR (internal or external). Editable allows in-memory editing but doesn't write back. Read-Only prevents modification. Requestor is a scope, not an edit mode.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to save data from a savable Data Page to an external REST API. Which data save option is correct?

options.text: Connector — saves to external SOR via REST-based integration
Database save — saves a single page to a database row
Robotic Automation — unattended RPA for external system writes
Activity — custom persistence logic via an Activity Rule

practiceQuiz.hint: Saving to an external REST API uses the Connector save option, not Database save.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Connector option saves to external SORs using REST integration. Database save writes to an internal Pega database. Robotic Automation is for systems with no API. Activity is for custom logic and should be limited.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When is a Lookup used as the source for a savable Data Page operation?

options.text: When a key is present — the record exists and needs to be updated
When no key is present — creating a new record for the first time
When the Data Page uses list structure instead of page structure
When the SOR is Pega Platform's internal database

practiceQuiz.hint: Key IS present = existing record = use Lookup as the Data Page source.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Lookup is used when the key is present (updating an existing record). Data Transform is used when the key is absent (creating a new record). C and D are not the determining factors for source selection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO methods can trigger the save plan for a savable Data Page?

options.text: Add a Save Data Page Automation Step in a flow Rule
Add post-processing for a Flow Action Rule
Configure a Stage validation in the Case Life Cycle
Set the Data Page scope to Thread

practiceQuiz.hint: 3 trigger methods: Automation Step, Flow Action post-processing, Activity Save-DataPage method.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A (Save Data Page Automation Step in a flow) and B (Flow Action post-processing) are both documented trigger methods. The third is calling Save-DataPage in an Activity Rule. C (Stage validation) and D (Thread scope) are unrelated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A form field is auto-populated from a savable Data Page. The user edits the field. To ensure the save plan can push changes to the SOR, how must the autopopulation be configured?

options.text: Refer to a Data Page — keeps the live connection so the save plan sees the changes
Copy data from a Data Page — stores the value for the save plan to read
Either Refer or Copy — both work the same for savable Data Pages
Copy data — required specifically when using the Database save option

practiceQuiz.hint: Auto-populated property sourced from a savable Data Page: always REFER, never copy.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Refer to a Data Page' keeps the property connected to the savable Data Page — edits made by the user are reflected in the Data Page and the save plan can push them to the SOR. Copy creates a snapshot; edits after the copy are invisible to the save plan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where should the Save Data Page Automation Step be placed in a flow relative to an Assignment?

options.text: After the Assignment — saves data after the user has entered or updated information
Before the Assignment — pre-populates the SOR before the user sees the form
At the start of the flow — saves data when the Case is created
At the end of the flow only — saves when the Case resolves

practiceQuiz.hint: Place the Save Data Page Step AFTER the user enters data in their Assignment.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The step is placed AFTER an Assignment so data is saved after the user enters or updates it. Placing it before saves stale or empty data to the SOR.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to commit updated data to TWO different external REST APIs in one flow. How is this configured?

options.text: Add two separate Save Data Page Automation Steps — one per external API
Configure a single Save Data Page Step with both APIs listed as targets
Use Aggregate sources in the save plan to write to both APIs simultaneously
Use a When Condition in the save plan to alternate between the two APIs

practiceQuiz.hint: One Save Data Page Step = one SOR commit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: To commit to multiple SORs, add multiple Save Data Page Automation Steps — one per SOR. A single step handles one data source only. B and C don't reflect how multi-SOR commits are documented.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Save Data Page Automation Step references a Data Page implicitly. What must the SA configure?

options.text: 'Use associated property' — select an autopopulated property; its associated Data Page is referenced automatically
The Data Page Name field — enter the Data Page name directly
'Copy data from Data Page' — specify the source Data Page
The Audit Note field — specify the SOR to write to

practiceQuiz.hint: Implicit Data Page reference selects 'Use associated property' to resolve automatically.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Use associated property' is the implicit option — select an autopopulated property and Pega resolves the associated savable Data Page automatically. B (Data Page Name) is the explicit option. C is a Data Page autopopulation setting. D mischaracterizes the Audit Note field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which database save option removes a record from the internal SOR as part of a transactional operation?

options.text: Database delete
Database update
Database save
Connector

practiceQuiz.hint: Which database save operation removes an existing record from the system of record?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The implicit reference option uses the property's associated savable Data Page. The explicit option requires entering the Data Page name directly. Both allow adding an Audit Note.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Pega Platform automatically manages transaction handling when the save plan is triggered from which source?

options.text: From a flow Rule or Flow Action — Pega manages transaction handling automatically
From an Activity Rule only — Activities provide built-in transaction management
All three trigger methods manage transactions identically
Transaction management must always be configured manually by the SA

practiceQuiz.hint: Flow or Flow Action triggers = automatic transaction handling.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When triggered from a flow Rule or Flow Action (post-processing), Pega automatically manages transaction handling. B and C are incorrect. D is wrong — automatic handling is available via flow/Flow Action triggers.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A savable Data Page must support both creating new customer records and updating existing ones. Which sourcing approach is correct?

options.text: Conditional: Lookup when key exists (update); Data Transform when key absent (create)
Always use Data Transform — it handles both create and update
Always use Lookup — it creates new records when none exist
Create two separate savable Data Pages — one for create, one for update

practiceQuiz.hint: Key present → Lookup (update). Key absent → Data Transform (create).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conditional sourcing on a single savable Data Page: Lookup when the record exists, Data Transform when creating new. B and C each handle only one operation. D is unnecessarily complex.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a Savable Data Page to write customer address updates back to an external CRM system and needs to verify the available save options and how the save is triggered. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Savable Data Pages are configured to write data?

options.text: Savable Data Pages can write to both Pega Platform's internal database and external SORs
The Connector save option supports both REST and SOAP integrations
When Conditions in the data save plan allow committing to multiple data tables
The save plan can only be triggered by a Save Data Page Automation Step

practiceQuiz.hint: Connector = REST only. 3 trigger methods, not 1.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A is correct — savable Data Pages work for both internal and external SORs. C is correct — When/Otherwise conditions in the save plan enable multi-table commits. B is wrong — Connector is REST only (not SOAP). D is wrong — there are 3 trigger methods.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is configuring a Savable Data Page to write updated customer contact information back to an external CRM system. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Savable Data Pages work?

options.text: A Savable Data Page is configured with data save options that define how and where the data is written back to the system of record
A Save Data Page Automation Step in the Case workflow explicitly triggers the save plan to commit the changes to the external system
A Savable Data Page automatically writes all changes to the source system whenever any property on the page is modified
The Save Data Page Automation Step must always be placed in the first Step of the first Stage to function correctly

practiceQuiz.hint: Savable Data Pages define how to write data; a Save Data Page step explicitly triggers the write at the.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Savable Data Pages are configured with save options that describe the connector and operation to write data back to the source system. The actual write is triggered explicitly by a Save Data Page Automation Step in the workflow — data is not automatically written on every property change.

quickRecap.value: Pushes data FROM Data Page TO SOR (Pega or external). Edit mode = Savable. Requires a data save plan.
Database save (page + Data Transform), Database update, Database delete, Connector (REST only), Robotic Automation, Robotic Desktop Automation, Activity (limit use).
Page structure only (not list). Requires Data Transform mapping. Transactional integrity.
① Save Data Page Automation Step in flow (after Assignment). ② Flow Action post-processing. ③ Save-DataPage Activity method.
Key present → Lookup (update existing). Key absent → Data Transform (create new).
Must use 'Refer to Data Page' — NOT Copy. Refer keeps the live connection for the save plan.
Add multiple Save Data Page Steps to the flow — one per SOR.
Explicit = Data Page Name field. Implicit = 'Use associated property' (resolves automatically).
